crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Routing Across Automated Market Makers
children.blurb: Routing across automated market makers is the practice of finding and executing a trade across one or more decentralised exchange pools rather than sending the entire order to a single venue.

children.name: Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Yield strategies in smart contracts are automated programs that move deposited capital across decentralised finance protocols to earn returns from lending, liquidity provision, staking, and arbitrage.

children.name: On-Chain Forensics
children.blurb: On-chain forensics is the practice of examining blockchain transaction records to trace the movement of digital assets, attribute addresses to real-world entities, and reconstruct financial activity across crypto markets and decentralised finance protocols.

children.name: Stablecoin Stress Testing
children.blurb: Stablecoin stress testing examines how a stablecoin maintains its peg and meets redemptions under adverse market conditions, including runs, collateral devaluation, liquidity freezes, and operational failures.

children.name: Governance Token Outcomes
children.blurb: Governance token outcomes refers to the measurable results of holding and using tokens that confer voting rights in decentralized protocols, including price performance, voting participation, treasury allocation, and protocol changes.

sections.body: This field covers how artificial intelligence is used in cryptocurrency trading, decentralised finance protocols, and the analysis of blockchain data. In practice, AI models now route trades across automated market makers to reduce price impact, scan smart contracts for yield opportunities, and flag suspicious wallet activity for compliance teams. They also run simulations of stablecoin redemptions and model voting behaviour in decentralised autonomous organisations. The work is operational, not speculative: models are trained on order books, liquidity pools, transaction graphs and governance proposals. The site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, a concrete sign of this overlap.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The most reliable results are in narrow, data-rich tasks like trade routing and on-chain forensics, where patterns repeat and labels exist. Yield strategy models can backtest well but often fail when liquidity dries up or a protocol changes its incentives. Stablecoin stress testing remains limited by the lack of historical depegging events, so simulations rely on assumptions that may not hold in a real run. Governance token outcome prediction is still early, because voting behaviour is noisy and easily influenced by a few large holders. Honest limits include poor generalisation across chains, vulnerability to adversarial manipulation of on-chain data, and the fact that many DeFi models are not audited for safety.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with Routing Across Automated Market Makers to see how AI chooses paths through liquidity pools, then move to Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts for how those paths are turned into recurring returns. On-Chain Forensics explains the detection side, using the same transaction data to trace illicit flows and sanction evasion. Stablecoin Stress Testing connects the market structure to systemic risk, showing what happens when redemptions spike. Governance Token Outcomes closes the loop by examining how the people and bots who hold voting power actually steer these protocols. Together the pages move from execution to risk to control.
